normative_action: Vocabulary: a must/must-not violation is a defect; a deviation from a 'default' needs a concrete reason and must be reported; prefer/avoid are guidance; 'requires approval' marks a Reserved decision.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Reporting obligation for default deviations is not in the oracle.

normative_action: A non-empty SPECIFICATION.md is authoritative for project-specific functional requirements and observable behaviour; the template file is intentionally empty.
Must not silently weaken, contradict or materially extend specified behaviour or invent user-visible behaviour, limits, defaults, restrictions or workflows, even when they seem reasonable.
When an omitted detail materially affects observable behaviour propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval.
Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behaviour need no approval.
Observable string semantics (case sensitivity, collation, culture vs ordinal, normalization, trimming, uniqueness, lookup) are product behaviour; choosing them when undefined requires approval.
Approved tunable limits and defaults live in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, which never overrides SPECIFICATION.md (behavioural intent).
The two files must not contradict; on apparent conflict stop and ask which source must be corrected; never choose silently.
Must not silently invent a material tunable value: propose it, obtain approval, record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
After recording an approved tunable value synchronize it (custom-settings).
Must not store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers or incidental implementation constants in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
Product, feature and task inputs may request a decision change but must not silently override engineering policy or recorded decisions.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Product-input vs engineering-policy precedence not stated in the oracle.

normative_action: Classify a choice (Decided, Delegated, Reserved) before acting on it.
Decided choices (decision register, standards, specification, established project structure) are followed; reopening requires approval.
Decided approved technology is followed rather than replaced by an alternative without approval.
Delegated choices (local, reversible, no material boundary/dependency/convention/contract/behaviour change) are decided and implemented.
Reserved choices require explicit approval before implementation; the list is a minimum.
Changing an accepted project or architecture decision, including a capability selection, is Reserved.
New architectural styles/patterns are Reserved: CQRS, mediators, VSA, event sourcing, microservices, Rich Domain/DDD tactical patterns, a project-wide Result model.
Adding a production project, layer or assembly is Reserved.
Changing the project reference graph is Reserved.
Changing persistence boundaries (e.g. multiple persistence contexts) or persistence technology is Reserved.
Adding messaging, background-processing or distributed-cache infrastructure is Reserved.
Adding search, external storage or external identity infrastructure is Reserved.
Adding a major library or framework is Reserved.
why_extra_or_uncertain: The oracle requires a concrete need, not approval.

normative_action: Replacing approved baseline technology is Reserved.
Introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction that other code is expected to follow is Reserved.
Changing authentication/authorization architecture is Reserved.
A breaking public API change is Reserved.
Adopting API versioning is Reserved.
why_extra_or_uncertain: API-013 requires a concrete need, not approval.

normative_action: Defining product behaviour or tunable values the product sources do not define is Reserved.

Unclear case: any 'yes' to the five questions (dependency/framework/infrastructure, project/layer/reference boundary, convention, observable behaviour/public contract, expensive to reverse) makes it Reserved.
Do not escalate routine local decisions already constrained by the specification, decision register, existing code or standards.
For a Reserved choice raise a Decision Request through architecture-decision and do not implement it before approval.
An explicit user instruction counts as approval; the accepted decision must still be recorded through architecture-decision.
In autonomous/headless runs take only a policy-compliant non-Reserved path, never silently make or alter a Reserved decision, and report every unresolved Decision Request.
Default to the simplest maintainable solution with proportional complexity and no speculative abstractions.
Must not introduce frameworks, libraries, infrastructure or architectural patterns without a concrete current need.
Changes stay within the requested scope and preserve existing behaviour unless the task or approved specification requires a change.

Before implementing a questionable request name the concrete concern (duplication, cohesion, trigger/loading problems, context cost, architecture/policy conflict, unnecessary complexity) and propose an alternative; never silently rewrite or ignore the requirement.
Must not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete branches or run any other repository-changing Git operation unless explicitly requested; requested operations follow git-workflow.
Parallel implementation work uses separate branches or worktrees; unrelated changes stay out of the current branch.
Implementing a feature, fix, refactor or new application runs development-workflow.
Completing implementation work runs verify.
Changes to this instruction system are governed by template-maintenance, which is user-invoked only.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system maintenance gate not in the oracle.

normative_action: Changes to CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md go through custom-settings; file rules are in CLAUDE.md (Product sources).
Only genuinely shared .NET build settings in Directory.Build.props; project-specific settings stay in their projects.
Shared target framework net10.0.
Shared build settings Nullable enable and ImplicitUsings enable.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Concrete compiler settings not in the oracle.

normative_action: Central versions are added by add-dependency after registry, license and vulnerability checks; never copy versions from examples.
ManagePackageVersionsCentrally is enabled.
Register entries are Decided and followed; changing any entry is Reserved and goes through architecture-decision.

Static composition: exactly one implementation per required capability slot and zero or one for the optional slot; unselected implementations are not part of the runtime; each module manifest lists its facets.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Capability-slot composition rule not in the oracle.

normative_action: Selected architecture: clean-architecture with backend roles Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Api as backend/<Name>.<Layer>/.
Not adopted: CQRS handlers, MediatR, Kommand, VSA or similar mediator-based organization; introducing them requires explicit approval.
Selected persistence: EF Core with SQL Server (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer); provider concerns stay out of Application and Domain; EF Core migrations; dedicated Development seeder.
String comparison follows database collation (SQL Server defaults are case-insensitive); observable semantics remain a product decision.
Selected backend testing: NUnit; test projects beside production projects under backend/; WebApplicationFactory<Program> integration baseline; Testcontainers conditional.
Selected optional frontend: current stable Angular with compatible TypeScript/RxJS, standalone, strict, routing, zoneless when supported, SCSS, Material/CDK, Vitest.
Not added by default: NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap, Tailwind or additional form/component/state libraries; built-in Angular first; extras only for a concrete need.
Use the approved technology; must not silently select an alternative; replacing approved technology requires approval.
.NET 10 LTS, C# 14, ASP.NET Core, Controllers; preview/RC requires approval.
FluentValidation is the standard explicit request/use-case validation library.
Application code logs through ILogger<T>; Serilog is the provider.
Swashbuckle Swagger UI is the default Development documentation/testing surface (not built-in AddOpenApi()/MapOpenApi()); outside Development only when requirements justify it.
.slnx by default; legacy .sln only when an external tool or requirement needs it.
Repository-level Directory.Build.props for shared build settings and Directory.Packages.props for CPM; project-specific settings stay in their projects.
Conditional technologies are approved but added only when the capability is actually needed.
Manual mapping for simple cases; Mapster when mapping volume warrants it.
Microsoft resilience packages only when a real integration needs resilience.
Playwright when E2E coverage is required; not part of the baseline scaffold.
Must not introduce Docker merely because the application can be containerized; container artifacts only when the project or deployment needs them.
Production and backend test projects in backend/<Name>.<Layer>/, frontend workspace in frontend/<Name>.Web/, documentation in docs/; no top-level tests/ directory.
Accepted decisions are recorded in the register by architecture-decision, with optional detailed records in docs/decisions/.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Decision-recording mechanism not in the oracle.

normative_action: The code-reviewer agent disallows Write, Edit and NotebookEdit.
exceptions: MultiEdit and shell tools are not disallowed.

normative_action: Run the code-review workflow on the requested scope and return its report; do not edit files or redefine review criteria (the workflow and the standards it loads are authoritative).

The architecture slot is a required frame with exactly one implementation that binds no slot and defines the stable role vocabulary; placement belongs to the frame and technique to the leaves; an implementation must provide role map, dependency direction, domain modeling, use-case orchestration, commit-boundary placement, composition root, transport contracts, test-project placement, not-adopted styles, scaffold layout and a deterministic reference check.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Capability contract not in the oracle.

why_extra_or_uncertain: Facet-role convention not in the oracle.

normative_action: The backend-testing slot is a required leaf with exactly one implementation bound to the architecture frame; the framework-neutral testing standard stays unchanged on replacement and the knowledge facet keeps the name dotnet-testing; an implementation must provide a framework standard, integration-host binding, knowledge, test scaffold and a check flagging additional test frameworks.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Capability contract not in the oracle.

normative_action: The frontend slot is an optional leaf with zero or one implementation ('none' means no workspace, no facets and a register row recording none) in frontend/<Name>.Web/; neutral frontend standards stay unchanged on replacement; an implementation must provide stack properties, framework standard, knowledge, workspace scaffold and a package.json library check; with 'none' the facet locations are absent and pointers to them stay dormant.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Capability contract not in the oracle.

normative_action: The persistence slot is a required leaf with exactly one implementation and one provider variant, bound to the architecture frame; an implementation must provide technology boundary, commit-boundary binding, migration mechanism, seeding mechanism, provider variant, declared properties (e.g. string comparison), testing implications, change workflow, knowledge and enforcement.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Capability contract not in the oracle.

normative_action: EF Core types live only in the Infrastructure role; UnitOfWork implements the Application IUnitOfWork over the shared scoped AppDbContext; persistence code sits in Infrastructure/Persistence/.
Never hardcode or commit real secrets, credentials, private keys, access/refresh tokens or production connection strings, including in example configuration files.
Local secret mechanism (dotnet user-secrets) for development and environment-specific injection or a managed secret store when deployed; do not assume an unchosen cloud provider.
Data crossing the trusted boundary (requests, uploads, external responses, message payloads, user-provided identifiers/filters) is untrusted and validated at the owning layer when assumptions matter.
Authorization is enforced on the server; route guards, hidden/disabled UI actions and client checks are UX, not a security boundary.

Production traffic carrying credentials or sensitive data uses TLS, respecting the hosting topology (in-app redirection not required where the deployment provides the boundary and redirection is not desired).
Never disable certificate validation to make an integration work.

Never log passwords, tokens, private keys, authentication secrets or full payment credentials; avoid PII without a concrete permitted operational need; a lower log level does not make sensitive data safe; prefer stable technical identifiers.
Do not serialize arbitrary request bodies, domain objects or sensitive payloads into logs by default; log minimal useful non-sensitive context.
Security-sensitive authorization, permission and required-control checks fail safely; never silently convert a lookup or configuration failure into success.
A required security control that cannot be configured correctly fails visibly at startup/configuration time instead of falling back to an insecure mode.
Physical structure follows responsibilities: no speculative projects, infrastructure, empty directory trees or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets to look architectural.
Add a dependency only for a concrete current requirement, never for hypothetical future use; an approved technology is not a reason to install it by default.
ASP.NET Core Controllers are the default HTTP entry point and stay thin: bind and validate input, invoke Application services, translate outcomes into HTTP responses.
Controllers contain no business logic, do not access the database context or concrete repositories and do not construct infrastructure services manually.
Constructor injection for required dependencies; avoid service-locator and property injection.
Dependency lifetimes are valid; never capture a shorter-lived dependency in a longer-lived service.
Cache technology stays out of Domain; infrastructure cache APIs do not leak into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.
Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into Application-facing abstractions; HttpResponseMessage and transport concerns never leak into Application.

Role map: Domain (backend/<Name>.Domain, business concepts independent of infrastructure and transport), Application (use-case orchestration and abstractions), Infrastructure (implementations of Application abstractions), Api (HTTP entry point and composition root).

Dependencies point inward (Domain none; Application→Domain; Infrastructure→Application, Domain; Api→Application and Infrastructure only for composition/registration); inner layers never depend on outer layers or Infrastructure-specific types.
If a feature seems to need an outward reference, reconsider the abstraction boundary instead of adding it.
Domain stays independent of the persistence technology, ASP.NET Core, HTTP and external-service implementation concerns.
Simple domain entities; straightforward CRUD and workflow rules (validation, immutable fields, status transitions, edit rules) belong in Application Services and do not justify a richer model.

Move behaviour into Domain only for non-trivial invariants materially benefiting from encapsulation; otherwise Rich Domain/DDD tactical patterns require approval unless the specification requires them.
No factories, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar merely to look domain-driven.
In an approved DDD design Aggregate Roots are the natural repository-boundary candidates.
Application Services orchestrate use cases (Domain objects, repositories, external abstractions, Unit of Work); a large service signals reconsidering responsibilities, not another pattern.
Application defines the persistence and external-service abstractions its use cases require and keeps infrastructure details out.
Application must not depend on persistence-technology types or APIs (database context, entity sets, query/provider types) or ASP.NET Core transport types.
IUnitOfWork is the use-case commit boundary; repositories stage changes and Application Services decide when to commit.
Repositories in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence context, are injected explicitly, and IUnitOfWork never becomes a repository container or service locator.
Program.cs in Api is the composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations.
Registration stays near the owning layer (AddApplication, AddInfrastructure(configuration)); Api composes them.
Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across Api and Application merely for layer-shaped types; transport-specific contracts in Api when separation gives a concrete boundary benefit.
Specific repository interfaces for cohesive Application persistence needs, defined in Application and implemented in Infrastructure, not table-mirroring generic CRUD.
Repository interfaces never expose IQueryable<T>, database-context or entity-set types, query expressions or provider types; return materialized entities, collections, projections or result models.
Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T> or another generic CRUD contract; a generic base only as an Infrastructure detail removing real duplication.
Database access is parameterized (raw SQL, micro-ORMs, ADO.NET included); never build SQL by concatenating untrusted input.
An empty Development database receives a small deterministic representative seed dataset covering meaningful states and relationships.
Automatic seeding runs only in Development, never Production; the development seeder is not test setup; tests own their setup.
When representative data exists leave it unchanged; never use the seeder to synchronize, repair, upgrade, overwrite or recreate an existing Development database; developers recreate explicitly.
Seed entities preserve Domain invariants and valid relationships; prefer readable deterministic examples over exhaustive or random combinations.
EF Core is an Infrastructure detail used fully there; DbContext, DbSet<T>, EF Core APIs, EF-backed IQueryable<T> and provider types never leak into Application.
Infrastructure implements IUnitOfWork by delegating to the shared scoped AppDbContext.
No explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case needs control beyond a single SaveChangesAsync.
Development seeding is an Infrastructure/bootstrap concern and may use AppDbContext directly without repositories or IUnitOfWork.

Substantial seed construction lives in a dedicated internal DbSeeder (Persistence/Seeding/) behind a narrow Infrastructure initialization extension, never in Program.cs, AppDbContext configuration, entity configurations or migrations.
The development seeder must not call Database.Migrate()/EnsureCreated() or otherwise create/upgrade schema; migrations are applied separately before seeding.
appsettings.Development.json provides a usable local connection string when it holds no secret credentials; credential-bearing values come from user-secrets or another approved local mechanism.
HTTP status codes and transport semantics belong to the Api layer; Application/Domain never return IActionResult or ASP.NET Core status codes.
Success statuses follow HTTP semantics: never 200 for every outcome, 201 for an internal insert or 202 for completed work.
A successful zero-match collection query returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.
401 for missing/failed authentication, 403 for a non-permitted principal; 404 hiding requires a deliberate consistent security policy.
409 for valid requests conflicting with current state; 412 when an explicit HTTP precondition such as If-Match fails.
ProblemDetails for non-validation failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation; machine-readable contracts stable and safe.
Unexpected failures propagate to centralized IExceptionHandler handling; avoid repetitive catch/log/rethrow.
Never expose stack traces, SQL, connection strings, internal paths, secrets or sensitive exception details in public API errors.
Log an unexpected exception once at the handling boundary; never again across repository, Application, controller and global handler.
Normal client-request cancellation is not mapped to a generic 500 or logged as an unhandled failure.
Represent expected outcomes explicitly when useful (null, bool, typed outcome); no forced Result<T>; no HTTP-named outcome categories in Application.

FluentValidation for explicit request/use-case validation where appropriate; validation at its owning boundary (Api transport, Application use-case rules, Domain invariants, Infrastructure external assumptions); no mechanical duplication across layers.
Business exceptions are not the default architecture; never throw/catch merely to jump between expected branches.
Must not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; only for published compatibility or coexisting client generations (adopting it is Reserved).
A version relied on by external clients must not change incompatibly in silence; a breaking change needs a new version or an explicitly approved compatibility strategy.
When explicit versioning is required use one strategy consistently, URL-segment unless requirements justify another.
No separate Domain or persistence models merely because the external API has multiple versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the Api boundary.
Swagger/OpenAPI metadata describes the running API (routes, important statuses, schemas, authentication) and never speculative responses.
Swagger UI enabled in Development and exposed elsewhere only when a deployment requirement explicitly justifies it.
Health checks stay cheap and deterministic, never business workflows or expensive/mutating database work.
Liveness avoids external dependencies whose unavailability could cause restart loops; readiness may depend on required capabilities and must reflect startup and dependency availability.
Publicly reachable health responses never expose secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces or unnecessary diagnostics.
ILogger<T> with structured templates and stable property names; avoid interpolation that makes structured values opaque.
When Serilog is configured use DI-integrated AddSerilog with environment-aware provider configuration; application code depends on ILogger<T>.
Strongly typed options validated at startup when missing/invalid values prevent correct or secure operation; avoid scattered string-based IConfiguration lookups.
Production containers use an appropriate runtime image, not the SDK image for convenience, and do not switch to root to bypass filesystem problems.
Anonymous access is deliberate and visible; avoid redundant authorization attributes when a secure global or fallback policy expresses the intent.
No custom token/password security, password hashing or reset-token cryptography when ASP.NET Core authentication/Identity covers the requirement.
Bearer/OIDC validates what the issuer/provider requires (issuer, audience where applicable, signature/signing authority, lifetime); never disable validation to make a token work.
Authentication failures never reveal secrets or account state unnecessarily; login avoids account-enumeration leaks where relevant.
No custom cryptography when a reviewed platform mechanism fits; Data Protection is not universal database encryption.
Narrowest CORS policy for actual browser clients (a public unauthenticated API may differ); never credentialed cross-origin requests with unrestricted origins.
Never treat client-provided file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative when handling or security depends on actual content.
Clear correct code first; no specialized optimization without a concrete reason; measurement/profiling evidence for non-trivial optimizations.
Compiled queries, ValueTask, pooling, custom serialization, aggressive caching and raw SQL for performance only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need.
Use async APIs for asynchronous I/O; never block with .Result, .Wait() or similar.
Propagate CancellationToken when cancellation is meaningful; no cancellation parameters on purely synchronous code without a use case.
TimeProvider for clock-dependent logic needing deterministic tests; no mechanical replacement of explicit or stored timestamps.
Filter and project in the database when practical; avoid unnecessary round trips, over-fetching and N+1; paginate potentially large results.
Never create and dispose an HttpClient per request; use IHttpClientFactory or another long-lived strategy.
External I/O calls have bounded execution time; avoid overlapping timeout mechanisms with unclear combined behaviour.
Retry only when repetition is safe; never automatically retry state-changing operations without idempotency or another concrete safety mechanism.
Respect Retry-After or equivalent rate-limit guidance where appropriate; never retry indefinitely or aggressively.
Use a fallback only when semantically acceptable; never hide correctness failures behind convenient defaults.
Caller cancellation is not a transient failure: never retry it or turn it into repeated outbound attempts.
No caching without a clear measured or reasoned need; choose the implementation by deployment, consistency and staleness requirements.
Cache keys uniquely represent the value including user, tenant and context dimensions; no global keys for user- or tenant-specific data.
Every cache entry has a lifetime or another explicit invalidation strategy.
Invalidate/update cache entries only consistently with successful mutations; the cache never becomes a second source of truth.
Follow existing conventions and .editorconfig; modern C# when it improves clarity; do not rewrite working code solely for newer syntax.
New C# code: file-scoped namespaces when consistent; one primary top-level type per matching file; Async suffix on Task/ValueTask methods unless a contract makes it inappropriate.
No style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked; avoid mixing large formatting/modernization with functional work.

normative_action: NUnit is the default .NET test framework; an established project deliberately using another follows it; no second framework without a concrete reason.
Backend test projects never have broader production references than their test scope requires and follow the inward dependency discipline.

Typical references: Domain.Tests (optional) → Domain; Application.Tests → Application (Domain as needed); IntegrationTests → Api (other layers through the host); Infrastructure.Tests (optional) → Infrastructure and narrower references as required.
Narrowest meaningful test level; integration tests when wiring, HTTP, persistence, serialization or authentication is the subject; no fixed ratio.

Tests verify observable behaviour, survive refactoring, do not test private calls or call sequences, do not reproduce the algorithm; interaction verification only when the interaction is the specified behaviour.
WebApplicationFactory-based integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, auth, DI, repositories, persistence technology or database persistence must be proven.
Actual database provider when relational/provider behaviour matters (Testcontainers optional); never claim provider fidelity from a different provider.
Tests are deterministic, order-independent and isolated from Production/Development data, uncontrolled external systems and shared mutable state.
Tests start from a known state, own their setup and never depend on development seed data or test order.
Small finite spaces use explicit declarative cases instead of loops, branches, LINQ or generated machinery; expected results are stated, not computed.
Descriptive test names (e.g. MethodOrScenario_Condition_ExpectedBehavior) unless the project has a convention.
Must not generate low-value tests merely to increase coverage.

npm is the frontend package manager unless deliberately changed; package.json and package-lock.json are committed and consistent; build/test tooling belongs in devDependencies unless there is a concrete reason.

normative_action: Modern standalone Angular APIs for new code (no new NgModules for ordinary features), organized primarily by feature.
Signals for synchronous local UI state; RxJS for async streams, HTTP composition, cancellation or event pipelines; avoid mechanical conversions.
Functional HTTP interceptors for new code; interceptors stay cross-cutting and never contain feature business logic.
Reactive forms for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation is UX and never replaces backend validation or integrity/security enforcement.
Avoid manual nested RxJS subscriptions; prefer composition operators.
Manual subscriptions from framework-managed code are tied to the component/service lifecycle with current Angular facilities (e.g. takeUntilDestroyed).
Feature-oriented structure: no application-wide technical buckets or empty architecture folders; feature code stays in its feature; core/shared stay small.
Pages and components focus on presentation and UI orchestration; no moving trivial presentation logic into services merely to shrink components.
Route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; not for every tiny component.
Simple local, component or feature-service state before a state-management library.

Backend communication lives in explicit feature data-access services or another HTTP boundary; never scattered HTTP calls; never backend Domain types in the frontend; frontend API models match the published contract.
Follow the documented API error contract; centralize ProblemDetails parsing when practical; never infer business behaviour from human-readable messages.
When browser cookies carry authentication automatically CSRF protection is part of the design; the SPA framework does not remove the risk; explicit Bearer headers differ.
Never claim one browser token-storage mechanism is universally secure; choose by threat model; never log tokens.

Application defines persistence contracts (specific repositories, IUnitOfWork); Infrastructure implements them with EF Core; IUnitOfWork is the Application-facing abstraction over DbContext's commit boundary and delegates to the same scoped DbContext.
Keep entity configuration in separate IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> classes.
Keep persistence-specific configuration out of Domain entities where practical.
AddDbContext registers a scoped context shared by repositories and the Unit of Work in a request; use the selected provider, never one added because an example shows it.
Repositories stage changes; the Application Service calls IUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync once the operation is ready.
An Infrastructure-only base class may remove genuine duplication without becoming a generic CRUD contract; concrete repositories keep the full EF Core API.
Project in the database for read-only queries needing selected data; projection not mandatory when the entity is needed; avoid loading a complete aggregate for a few fields.
Tracking queries when entities will be modified and committed through the Unit of Work; AsNoTracking() for read-only entity queries; no mechanical AsNoTracking() on DTO projections.
Prefer an explicit query shape (projection or Include/ThenInclude); for large collection includes consider split queries and verify the generated SQL.
Avoid lazy loading by default (hidden database access, N+1).
Filter, order and page in the database.
Pagination always uses deterministic ordering.
ExecuteUpdateAsync/ExecuteDeleteAsync bypass change tracking: do not mix them casually with tracked entities for the same rows; understand transaction and consistency implications.
Never fire-and-forget EF Core asynchronous operations; a DbContext is not thread-safe.

One SaveChangesAsync is normally the transaction boundary; explicit transactions only when several operations or SaveChangesAsync calls must succeed atomically; EF transactions do not solve distributed transactions.
Compiled queries only for a measured hot path where compilation/cache-lookup overhead is material.
Before specialized optimization inspect round trips, columns, N+1, indexes, generated SQL, query plans, materialized volume and tracking overhead.
EF Core interceptors only for infrastructure-level cross-cutting behaviour with a clear benefit (e.g. auditing); never hide business behaviour in them.
Detect existing data with representative root/anchor entities; keep the seeder internal and expose a narrow extension that creates the scope.
Consider representative states (new, active, completed, archived, optional values/relationships, status values, boundary states).
When the required graph is complex the task should describe the dataset explicitly instead of inventing a large generic graph.
Create migrations from the Infrastructure project with the Api project as startup project.
For controlled production deployment generated idempotent migration scripts are often preferable; production migration is an explicit deployment step.
Raw SQL only when EF Core cannot express the query effectively or measured performance justifies it.
Keep raw SQL values parameterized (FromSql/FromSqlInterpolated, ExecuteSql/ExecuteSqlInterpolated); FromSqlRaw/ExecuteSqlRaw with concatenated input are unsafe.
String comparison follows the column/database collation (SQL Server defaults case-insensitive); choosing case sensitivity or collation is a product decision when observable.
Make an approved collation choice explicit with UseCollation(...) or a column-level collation.

Prefer provider execution strategies (EnableRetryOnFailure) over generic application retry pipelines, wrap explicit transactions in the execution strategy, and never apply HTTP retry policies to database operations.
The EF Core InMemory provider is not relational: never use it to claim relational behaviour; a fake repository is often clearer for unit tests.
Run provider-sensitive tests against SQL Server (e.g. Testcontainers MsSql or isolated LocalDB/SQL Server).
A lighter isolated relational database may suffice when provider specifics are irrelevant; state the trade-off.

Integration tests replace the registered DbContextOptions in WebApplicationFactory with an isolated test database and create the schema from migrations (EnsureCreated only for disposable test databases).

Test repository implementations and mappings when there is meaningful persistence behaviour (custom mappings, filters, projections, non-trivial queries, relationships, concurrency, provider behaviour).
Do not test every trivial Add/Get.
Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean, stash away or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier.
Before any repository-changing operation inspect the relevant state (status, diff, cached diff) and use the minimum operation; never silently clean unrelated changes.
reset --hard, clean, push --force, push --force-with-lease, branch deletion and rebasing shared history are performed only when explicitly requested or clearly required by an approved workflow.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Open question: GOV-015 permits repository-changing Git operations only when explicitly requested; whether 'clearly required by an approved workflow' widens that condition or only describes an explicitly requested workflow cannot be decided from the text.

normative_action: Inspect what will be lost or rewritten before a high-risk Git operation.
Before committing inspect the staged diff: only the intended logical change; never stage or clean unrelated modified files.
Prefer one logical change per commit with its tests; no artificial tiny commits or combined unrelated fixes and refactors.
Follow the branch-naming convention (feature/, fix/, refactor/, test/, docs/, chore/ as defaults); meaningful names; do not rename an existing user branch.
One branch is not checked out in multiple normal worktrees; each worktree stays focused on its branch's concern.
Before removing a worktree verify its changes are preserved; never remove a worktree containing uncommitted user work.
Follow the commit-message convention (Conventional Commits as default); use the body for motivation, constraints or migration notes; do not narrate obvious diff details.
Before pushing confirm the branch and understood state, ensure verification completed and avoid pushing unrelated local commits.
Never force-push a shared branch unless the user explicitly requests history rewriting and understands the consequences.
Treat main, master and other protected/shared branches as non-rewritable.
Inspect local uncommitted work first and never automatically stash, reset or discard it to let a merge/rebase proceed.

Follow the repository/team convention or the user's explicit request for merge vs rebase; resolve conflicts from the intended combined behaviour, not mechanically; run relevant verification afterwards.
Run verify before preparing a PR; a PR has a focused purpose and describes what changed, why, how it was verified and compatibility/migration notes.
Never claim checks that were not run.
Report the resulting Git state when useful (branch, commit, push target, PR status, remaining uncommitted changes).
Distinguish liveness from readiness when deployment infrastructure benefits from it.
Never make the application restart because a dependency is temporarily unavailable.
Include only dependencies required for meaningful readiness; keep readiness unhealthy until required startup work completes; never use liveness for this.
A database check is a lightweight connectivity/availability check (no business queries, large scans or data modification).
Check an external dependency only when its availability matters to readiness; prefer a lightweight check of the needed capability.
Avoid readiness cascades (A → B → C) without understanding their operational consequences.
Healthy → success, unhealthy → non-success per the configured probe policy (ResultStatusCodes); do not reuse business API status semantics mechanically.
Keep probe responses small; protect operator diagnostics with network or authorization controls instead of exposing connection strings, credentials, raw exceptions or topology.
Choose probe exposure by topology (private network, management port, host restrictions, supported authorization); probes often need unauthenticated infrastructure access.
Probes run frequently: avoid expensive queries, long external timeouts, large allocations and full workflows.
Avoid Error-level logs for every normal failed probe.

Test health configuration the deployment relies on (liveness responds, readiness follows required dependencies, no sensitive leaks, optional dependencies as intended); do not test uncustomized framework behaviour.
Health checks are not a code-quality grading system.

normative_action: Keep status-code behaviour consistent across similar endpoints.
200 OK: completed with a representation (GET, PUT/PATCH returning the representation, operation-style POST, queries).
Empty collections return 200 with [] (which preserves the representation better than 204).
201 Created: the HTTP operation created a new resource (Location when a stable URI exists; PUT may create); an inserted row alone is not creation.
202 Accepted: processing accepted but not complete (long-running operation, job, import, queue).
A 202 returns an operation identifier or a progress Location when practical.
204 No Content: completed with no body needed; a 204 response must not contain a body.
Choose consistently whether repeated DELETE of an absent resource returns 204 or 404; do not mix conventions between equivalent resources.
304 only for a conditional request whose cached representation is still valid; not a generic 'nothing changed' business response.

Status semantics beyond the oracle: 400 for invalid HTTP requests (never authentication failures); 406/415 for content negotiation and unsupported media types; 429 for rate limiting with Retry-After when known (never validation); 502/503/504 for intermediary, unavailability and upstream-timeout cases (not every dependency failure; 503 with Retry-After when meaningful).
401: authentication missing or failed; normally produced by authentication middleware.
403: authenticated but not allowed; deliberate 404 hiding only as a consistent policy.
404: the resource does not exist or is deliberately hidden; a zero-match collection query is not a 404.
409: a valid request conflicting with current state (duplicates, incompatible transitions, concurrent operations, reused idempotency key with a different payload); not for malformed syntax.
412: a supplied precondition is false (e.g. stale If-Match).
422 for structurally valid requests with invalid semantics; follow an established 400-for-both convention, otherwise new APIs use 400 for invalid contracts and 422 for invalid semantics.
428 when a contract-required precondition is omitted (missing If-Match → 428, stale → 412); other preconditions only when the contract makes them mandatory.
500 for unexpected failures without a more specific outcome, via centralized handling and ProblemDetails without stack traces, SQL, paths, credentials or exception details.
Distinguish client cancellation of the incoming request, own operation timeouts and upstream timeouts; not every TaskCanceledException is a 504.

GET safe/idempotent, PUT idempotent, DELETE idempotent in intended state, POST generally not; consider an Idempotency-Key for non-duplicating POSTs (different payload → 409); do not claim idempotency because duplicates are unlikely.
When HTTP optimistic concurrency is in the contract use standard conditional semantics (ETag/If-Match, 412 on mismatch, 428 when required and absent); do not replace them with custom status codes.
Application expresses outcomes without IActionResult, ProblemDetails or status codes; the controller maps them.
ProblemDetails for structured HTTP errors, ValidationProblemDetails for validation; clients rely on stable codes or contract fields, never human-readable messages.
Package defaults: Microsoft resilience integration; direct Polly only as a documented exception (add-dependency).
Resilience mechanisms are added only when failure and operation semantics justify them, and their behaviour is observed when it matters operationally.
The standard resilience handler fits when its behaviour matches the remote API, is not mandatory, and its retry behaviour is reviewed carefully for state-changing requests.
Do not stack resilience handlers with overlapping strategies.
The Microsoft packages build on Polly v8, but application code configures them through the Microsoft.Extensions resilience APIs.
Distinguish attempt timeout from total operation timeout, especially with retries.

Retry only plausibly transient failures; never retry validation, authentication/authorization failures, permanent 404, deterministic rejections or non-idempotent operations without duplicate prevention; for writes ask whether a lost response would cause duplicates; use an API-supported idempotency mechanism and never invent an unsupported Idempotency-Key.
Prefer respecting Retry-After when the policy supports it; never hammer a rate-limited dependency with an aggressive schedule.
Use a circuit breaker when repeated calls to a failing dependency would add load or latency, not without a meaningful repeated-failure pattern; give it operational visibility when it matters.
Valid fallbacks: acceptable stale cached reads, omitted optional enrichment; invalid: pretending a failed operation such as a payment succeeded.
Hedging only for operations safe to execute multiple times (typically idempotent reads against interchangeable endpoints); never for state-changing operations by default.
Do not wrap normal database operations in a generic application retry pipeline or apply HTTP retry policies to them; use provider-level transient-fault handling.
Retrying publication may duplicate delivery: use idempotent consumers, broker deduplication or an outbox when the business requires it; never claim exactly-once because a retry policy exists.
ASP.NET Core inbound rate limiting is separate from outbound resilience; rejected requests return 429 with Retry-After when a useful delay is known.
Propagate caller cancellation through resilience pipelines.
Observe retries, timeouts, circuit state, rate-limit rejections and latency with the adopted telemetry stack when they matter; OpenTelemetry is not required merely because pipelines exist.
Application may define an abstraction implemented in Infrastructure with HttpClient so Application does not know the service uses HTTP.
Named, typed and keyed clients are all valid; choose the model that makes ownership and lifetime easiest to understand; do not make one model mandatory universally.
Do not capture a transient typed client inside a singleton without understanding the lifetime implications.
Use DelegatingHandlers only for genuine HTTP pipeline concerns (authorization headers, correlation, signing), never for business decisions.
Pass the caller's token; use CancellationToken.None only when the operation intentionally must outlive the incoming request.
Choose time limits from the remote operation and latency budget; with resilience pipelines distinguish per-attempt from total timeout.
Translate remote responses into the abstraction Application consumes.
Do not blindly call EnsureSuccessStatusCode() when specific statuses carry contract meaning; map them explicitly.
Translate richer failures into explicit Infrastructure/Application outcomes and do not expose every upstream status through your API; outbound retry and the inbound response are separate decisions.

Before retrying determine transience, repeat safety, remote idempotency support and duplicate side effects; state-changing calls need idempotency keys, natural idempotency or deduplication; method semantics alone are not operational safety; a timeout is normally required, retry and circuit breakers are not mandatory.

Stable headers on the client; per-request values (dynamic tokens) on the request or via a handler, never by mutating shared DefaultRequestHeaders concurrently; prefer System.Net.Http.Json/System.Text.Json with explicit options when the external contract differs.
Never reuse Domain entities as remote API contracts to avoid mapping.
Serilog is the provider; application code keeps using ILogger<T>.
Use two-stage initialization (bootstrap logger) when startup logging before DI/configuration matters; simpler applications may use host-managed setup.
builder.Services.AddSerilog(), not builder.Host.UseSerilog(), integrating with DI via ReadFrom.Services.
Message templates, not interpolation ({PropertyName} creates queryable data; interpolation breaks structure and allocates).
Levels, sinks and overrides live in appsettings so they change per environment without redeployment.
Serilog APIs (Log.Logger, LogContext) stay at composition and provider-specific boundaries.

Serilog.AspNetCore is the baseline integration package; a Console sink suffices for a simple Development baseline; File, Seq, OpenTelemetry, Elasticsearch and enrichers are optional; example limits and retention values are illustrative.
Add sinks and enrichers only when the project requires them, through add-dependency.
Enrich request logs only with non-sensitive values.
Never destructure large graphs such as HttpRequest without limits; configure depth/string/collection limits or transform to specific properties.
Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch is deprecated; use Elastic.Serilog.Sinks.
When the static/bootstrap Log.Logger is used flush it on shutdown (CloseAndFlushAsync) so asynchronous sinks keep buffered events.
exceptions: Purely host-managed logging follows the provider lifetime.

normative_action: Stable property names keep logs queryable; log information that helps diagnose or operate the system.

Choose levels by operational meaning: Trace/Debug diagnostics (never assume sensitive data is safe there), Information meaningful events, Warning recovered/degraded conditions, Error failed operations needing investigation, Critical when the application or a subsystem cannot continue.
Log an exception at the boundary that handles or terminates the failure; when rethrowing without meaningful handling add no duplicate log.
Prefer platform trace identifiers; add an explicit correlation identifier only for an integration or operational requirement; propagate tracing context across outbound calls.
Validate or normalize a correlation identifier accepted from an external client.

Avoid logging authorization headers and full sensitive request/response bodies; log the specific properties needed; log level is not a privacy control; prefer technical identifiers over personal information.
Normal structured ILogger calls suffice; source-generated LoggerMessage only for measured high-volume hot paths, not everywhere to avoid theoretical allocations.
Do not use logs as an audit database (or AuditTo) unless a dedicated audit design was adopted.

normative_action: Use modern features when they make code clearer, safer or simpler; consistency and readability matter more than maximizing language features.
Prefer a regular constructor when validation/initialization is non-trivial, explicit fields read better, the codebase uses that style or parameter capture would obscure the class.
Never modernize working code mechanically (constructors, initializers, backing fields with clear logic).
Use collection expressions when the target type is clear.

Records for intentional value semantics (immutable DTOs, genuine Value Objects, immutable messages); classes for identity, mutable lifecycle, inheritance or framework behaviour; do not turn every DTO or Domain type into a record.
Use required when initialization is part of the valid construction contract, not as a substitute for constructor/domain validation protecting invariants.
Avoid deeply nested patterns that are harder to read than plain conditions.
Raw string literals are never a reason to introduce raw SQL.
var when the type is obvious or unimportant; an explicit type when it improves clarity; follow the project convention.
Standard .NET naming (PascalCase types/members, camelCase parameters/locals, meaningful names; private fields per repository convention).
Keep implementation details non-public unless part of the public API; sealed communicates deliberate design, not a speculative JIT optimization.
Do not reorganize an existing file merely to satisfy a preferred member ordering.
Immutability where it represents the model naturally; controlled mutation where framework models or workflows are simpler with it.
Span<T>, stackalloc, pooling and source-generated serialization for demonstrated hot paths with verified improvement; ordinary arrays, strings and collections are the default.
Confirm the configured language version supports a feature; never silently change LangVersion or the target framework (a platform change is Reserved).

Avoid record struct merely to avoid allocations.

normative_action: Create only directories that contain real code.
DDD-oriented directories (ValueObjects, DomainServices, Events, Exceptions) only when an approved design needs them; business rules or workflows alone do not justify them.

Application layout: Abstractions/Persistence without persistence-technology types, Abstractions/ExternalServices only once such dependencies exist, Services (Application Services), DTOs when useful (not a dumping ground), Validation (FluentValidation), AddApplication registering only Application services and validation.

Supporting type roles are clear from name and/or directory (established suffixes; e.g. TaskWorkflowRules over ambiguous TaskWorkflow); responsibility subdirectories only when a flat feature directory becomes hard to navigate.
Avoid generic Models, Helpers, Common or Utils buckets.

Infrastructure layout: Persistence (per persistence-change), Services implementing Application abstractions, AddInfrastructure(configuration) registering persistence, repositories, IUnitOfWork, adapters and HttpClient/resilience integrations when used.
Api layout: Controllers, Contracts, Middleware only when custom middleware exists, Extensions, Program.cs as composition root (AddApplication, AddInfrastructure).
Extensions hold cohesive composition extensions; do not move code just to shorten Program.cs.

Controllers are the HTTP endpoint mechanism (Minimal API groups only when explicitly requested); Api references Infrastructure only for composition and controllers never consume Infrastructure types; Contracts only when separation gives value.
Never add Domain→Application, Domain→Infrastructure or Application→Infrastructure; reconsider the abstraction boundary.
Test projects live beside production projects under backend/; create only useful ones.

Application.Tests → Application (+ Domain); IntegrationTests → Api; optional Domain.Tests only for non-trivial Domain behaviour; optional Infrastructure.Tests only for non-trivial Infrastructure behaviour.
A simple Domain needs no dedicated test project; integration tests reference Api for WebApplicationFactory<Program> and exercise the other layers transitively.

Use the latest stable Angular supported by the selected Node.js through the current CLI; let it select compatible Angular/TypeScript/RxJS; no independent TypeScript upgrade beyond the supported range.
Create the workspace in frontend/<Name>.Web.
Accept zoneless mode when supported; keep the CLI's Vitest runner or configure Vitest as the baseline for new projects.
Add Angular Material/CDK matching the workspace with ng add, following add-dependency for version and license checks.
Configure the API base URL for the Development backend compatible with the backend's CORS configuration.
Create feature directories only when they contain code; no empty core/shared/features trees.
Verify with the workspace's declared scripts (npm run build, npm test).
Commit package-lock.json.
Playwright E2E only when E2E coverage is required, inside frontend/<Name>.Web/e2e/.
The layout is a target structure; create optional directories or projects only when needed.
All backend .NET projects, including backend test projects, live under backend/.
The solution file uses .slnx.
The frontend workspace lives in frontend/<Name>.Web/ and owns its manifests and sources; frontend unit and E2E tests stay inside the workspace, never under backend/.
Do not impose an obsolete directory structure when the current framework CLI generates a different supported one.
docs/ subdirectories (architecture, decisions, api) only when the corresponding documentation exists.
Directory.Build.props holds genuinely shared settings (TargetFramework, Nullable, ImplicitUsings, analysis/compiler), never project-specific settings.
Directory.Packages.props holds NuGet CPM versions in one place.
global.json pins the intended supported SDK line (current stable SDK of the target release) with servicing per the chosen rollForward policy.
No RC/preview SDK unless explicitly requested.
.editorconfig holds deterministic repository-wide formatting/style; prefer enforceable tooling configuration over restating mechanical formatting rules in instructions.

Ignore generated/local artifacts (bin, obj, .vs, node_modules, dist, TestResults, coverage, local secret/config overrides, .claude/settings.local.json); do not ignore files intentionally part of the Development configuration contract.
Docker files, deployment manifests, Kubernetes, cloud, messaging and additional services only for a concrete requirement.
Create each useful test project from the NUnit template beside the production projects.
Under CPM move the template's package versions into Directory.Packages.props and keep references versionless (add-dependency resolves current stable versions).
Test packages: NUnit, NUnit3TestAdapter, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk and, for integration tests, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing; remove unused template packages.
Add only the production project references the test scope requires.
Integration tests expose Program to WebApplicationFactory<Program> when needed and configure an isolated Testing environment.
Testcontainers or other real-provider infrastructure only when provider fidelity requires it.
Build and run dotnet test to confirm the projects are discovered.

Goals: explicit boundaries, dependency direction through references, layout per the default, approved technology only, no speculative projects/abstractions/directories, an immediately buildable verified result.
Determine scope; do not scaffold optional infrastructure because it may be useful later (Docker only when containerization is needed).
Use the approved stack; conditional technologies only when required; resolve versions at install time through add-dependency, never copying versions from examples.
Create only required top-level directories and shared configuration files.
Create the four backend projects and only the listed references; never an outward reference to make compilation easier.

When frontend scope exists create the workspace under frontend/<Name>.Web/; frontend architecture belongs to the frontend standards and facet.
Only directories the initial implementation needs; no empty trees for hypothetical capabilities.
Development persistence via persistence-change; never add Production credentials or Production migration automation.

Verify: restore, build the solution and frontend, run relevant tests, inspect references with check-manifests, inspect the tree, confirm Development configuration, then verify; never report successful scaffolding that does not build.
Determine whether a new assembly is justified; a new production project or layer is Reserved.
Identify a new project's architectural/technical responsibility.
Add only the minimum required references, preserving dependency direction.
Update shared build/package configuration when necessary.
Build and test the affected solution after adding a project.
Never split code into additional projects merely to make the architecture look more sophisticated.

Reorganizing: inspect tree and references, identify a concrete structural problem, preserve behaviour, move in small reviewable steps, update namespaces/references consistently, avoid unrelated work, verify afterwards.
Do not force an established project to match this template when doing so provides no concrete value.

MediatR, CQRS trees, VSA, Domain Events, Specifications, SharedKernel, BuildingBlocks, EventBus, messaging, microservices, Kubernetes, cloud projects and state frameworks are not introduced by default; each requires an approved need.

Complete when structure matches scope, references respect the architecture, approved technology is used, no unnecessary projects/directories exist, builds and tests pass, Development configuration is usable and nothing unrelated was reorganized.
Do not upgrade packages during a scan unless asked; do not rate dependency findings from CVSS alone; consider reachability and exposure.
appsettings.Development.json is not automatically ignored: a real committed secret remains a secret; obviously fake values may be ignored or reported as Info; UserSecretsId is not a secret.
Safe forms: ORM LINQ, parameterized SQL, the persistence technology's interpolation-parameterizing APIs, ADO.NET/Dapper parameters; ordinary LINQ with user input in a predicate is not SQL injection.
Prefer APIs that separate executable and arguments; validate or constrain input when command execution is genuinely needed.
Normalize and verify that user-influenced paths remain within the intended storage boundary.
Untrusted payloads must not deserialize into arbitrary runtime types (e.g. BinaryFormatter, unsafe TypeNameHandling).

Flag security-sensitive MD5/SHA1/ECB, hardcoded keys, custom hashing and home-grown protocols (not non-security checksums); passwords use established hashers, not reversible encryption; never recommend custom cryptography.
Determine the effective authorization policy; an endpoint without explicit [Authorize] under a secure fallback is not automatically vulnerable; bare [Authorize] is not automatically insufficient.
Confirm deliberately public surfaces ([AllowAnonymous]) are intentional; not every public endpoint is a vulnerability.
Client-side filtering is not authorization.
Check that issuer, audience where applicable, signature/signing authority and lifetime are validated; flag intentionally disabled validation without valid reason.
Do not require manually setting every TokenValidationParameters property when authority/metadata configuration establishes secure validation, and do not impose an arbitrary universal ClockSkew.
Review local-account hashing, reset, lockout and enumeration behaviour; never recommend custom password hashing.
Route guards and hidden/disabled buttons are UX; verify sensitive operations are protected by the backend.

CORS is a browser-origin policy, not authorization; broad, credentialed-untrusted or Production-exposed environment origins are problems; AllowAnyOrigin can be valid for a public non-credentialed API; credentialed cross-origin access requires restricted origins.
When browser credentials (especially cookies) are sent automatically review CSRF protection for state-changing operations; do not assume the frontend framework provides server-side CSRF protection.

Disabled certificate validation, accept-all callbacks and plain HTTP for sensitive communication are findings, accounting for TLS termination; missing in-app redirection is not automatically a vulnerability.
Client-provided MIME types are not authoritative (review size limits, path safety, names, content assumptions, serving risks and authorization).
Consider rate limiting where abuse realistically matters (login/password reset, expensive anonymous endpoints, resource-intensive operations); do not require it on every endpoint.
Logs must not contain passwords, tokens, keys, auth secrets or full payment credentials; PII per project requirements; prefer technical identifiers; Debug/Trace is not a security boundary.
Prefer explicit response contracts where needed, but inspect the serialized fields before calling a returned entity a vulnerability.

Choose data-at-rest protection from the requirement (password hashing; hashed verification tokens; protected storage for retrievable secrets; platform/database encryption; Data Protection for temporary payloads, not universal database encryption; never custom cryptography).
Security-sensitive checks fail safely (no allow on failed authorization service, token validation or permission lookup).
Not every swallowed exception is a vulnerability, but security-relevant failures must not silently turn into success.
Review retries of state-changing operations for duplicate effects; caller cancellation is never retried.
A theoretical missing limit is not automatically High; evaluate whether an attacker can exploit it.
Prefer visible failure over insecure fallback in security-sensitive startup configuration (no silently disabled authentication, plaintext mode or allow-all).
When meaningful security-sensitive workflows exist, flag them for threat modeling or manual review instead of claiming the scan proves them secure.
Never map pattern, CVSS or OWASP category mechanically to severity.
Never invent exploitability the code does not establish.
The scan is an evidence-based static review, not a penetration test, and cannot prove the application secure; state that limitation in the report.

normative_action: Swashbuckle Swagger UI is the decided surface; the requirement is the interactive UI, not a standalone raw OpenAPI endpoint.
Keep Swagger configuration in the Api/composition layer.
Add Swashbuckle.AspNetCore through add-dependency.
Application HTTP/HTTPS URLs must agree with the launch profile; never point a browser launch URL to HTTPS on an HTTP-only port.

Document only statuses in the real runtime contract (never 201 for 200, 204 with a body, or speculative statuses), considering the whole pipeline (binding, validation, auth, rate limiting, exception handling, middleware).
For creation endpoints document 201 and prefer CreatedAtAction/CreatedAtRoute when a canonical URL exists.
Describe ProblemDetails/ValidationProblemDetails where useful.
Never expose internal exception types, stack traces, SQL, connection strings or paths in Swagger examples.
When the API uses authentication configure the matching security definition; no scheme merely because a package is installed; no global auth requirements on anonymous endpoints.
Document what helps consumers (preconditions, idempotency, pagination/filtering, outcomes), not name repetitions; XML comments only when the project chooses them, not on every internal type.
Use several documents only for a real contract separation (API versions, public/internal surfaces).
When the contract feeds client generation treat breaking schema changes seriously and keep metadata accurate.
Avoid unstable anonymous response shapes, use explicit request/response contracts and review generated-client changes when the contract changes.

When API behaviour changes verify controller behaviour, integration tests and metadata; start the API when startup changed, open the Development Swagger UI, exercise endpoints when meaningful and preserve newly verified behaviour in tests.
Swagger is not a substitute for integration tests.
why_extra_or_uncertain: No owner clause for this item.

normative_action: Implementation-specific content of a slot becomes a facet listed in the module manifest with 'Capability: <slot>/<implementation>'; implementation-independent slot policy stays in the neutral standard; placement belongs to the architecture frame, technique to leaves declaring frame bindings in Binds:.
A rule's paths include its scope's canonical glob (**/*, backend/**/*, backend/**/*Tests/**/*, frontend/**/*); no other directory hierarchy under .claude/rules/.
Every normative statement has exactly one owner; elsewhere only a routing pointer, a check-by-reference item or a register decision summary.

Keep the trigger role: always-loaded policy in OP/DEC, path policy in STD, procedure obligations in WF; do not move content between roles to save tokens; never place critical must-policy only in a skill.
Outside a module's facets, manifest, the register's selection block and the map, never name the selected implementation; facet file names are role-based.
Start each artifact with the header 'Kind | Scope | Capability | Loading' (after required frontmatter).
Skill frontmatter name equals the directory and the description is concise and trigger-first; WF bodies own procedure and output; KNW bodies own technique and point to standards for policy.
Capability changes follow architecture-decision (contract coverage, single implementation per slot, no unselected implementations at runtime).
Update the module manifest's facet table and both MAP views for every added, moved or removed artifact.

Hooks use exec form (node + [dispatch.cjs launcher, event]); the launcher only locates code while checks use the active root from the hook input cwd; the PreToolUse guard keeps onFailure block; post and Stop hooks stay advisory; hook messages point to owners.

ENF artifacts declare their policy owners on the line after the header ('Conforms: …' or '—') and every cited owner path is declared; slot bindings and facet roles are fixed; contract and manifest Binds agree.
Run check-instructions with the active root and fix every error; review the always-loaded size and keep it compact without moving required planning-time policy out.
Produce evidence that the change is complete without obvious regressions, matched to scope and risk, without requiring unconfigured optional tooling.

Review the final changed files and diff first: scope match without unrelated refactoring, temporary probes removed only after their behaviour is preserved, no generated/build artifacts, no secrets or environment credentials (remove any).
Determine affected areas (backend-only, frontend-only, contract/full-stack, documentation-only without unrelated builds).
Build the affected solution or projects; a build failure means the implementation is not complete.
For frontend changes inspect package.json and run the declared build script.
Do not use --no-restore unless restore is known to be complete.
Run tests covering the changed area and investigate every newly failing relevant test; never dismiss one as unrelated without checking.
Run the frontend's declared test script when one exists; inspect package.json rather than assuming a runner.
Small solutions run the full suite; large solutions run affected test projects first, then the broader suite required.

For new runnable applications or substantial composition/startup/configuration/persistence/full-stack changes verify Development startup (host, endpoint, Swagger UI, configuration binding, database initialization, frontend dev server, compatible API base URL and CORS); a build alone does not prove runtime composition.

Behaviour uniquely demonstrated by an ad-hoc/manual probe must be represented by maintained automated tests before completion unless confirmed equivalent coverage exists; builds, compilers, formatters, analysis and existing suites need no new tests.
Run architecture, formatting/analyzer, dependency and security checks when relevant, not indiscriminately.
Run checker commands by absolute path (node "<root>/.claude/scripts/<checker>.cjs", root from git rev-parse --show-toplevel or the directory holding CLAUDE.md and .claude/).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Command-form rule not in the oracle.

normative_action: For architecture-relevant changes read the architecture-style and persistence standards and run check-manifests.
When the persistence model changed confirm persistence-change was completed, including the development seeder for a freshly recreated database.
Run check-cochange for seed, migration and test reminders of the working tree.
Formatting/analyzer checks when configured; do not add a formatter or analyzer just to complete verification; analyzer output needs context.
For dependency or security-sensitive changes inspect vulnerabilities and changed secrets, authorization, raw SQL, CORS/TLS, sensitive logging and certificate validation.
When .claude/, CLAUDE.md or the register changed run check-instructions.
Review the final diff after all fixes for accidental unrelated edits and architecture drift.
Final diff review also checks commented-out code, temporary logging, unintended TODO/FIXME markers and stale temporary tests or scripts.
Check for unapproved drift from SPECIFICATION.md or CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
Check for stale code, tests, docs or configuration after a settings change.
Remove unused/redundant usings in every created or modified C# file (including implicit/global duplicates unless needed) without unrelated repository-wide cleanup; verify the changed files.
On failure identify it, make the smallest fix, rerun affected verification (and builds/tests when code changed), repeat until green or genuine user input is required.
Never hide a known failure and declare completion; persistent failures go to build-fix.
Report what was actually run using PASS / NOT RUN / NOT APPLICABLE; never imply that an unchecked area passed.
UTF-8, space indentation of 4 (2 for JSON/YAML/project/XML and TS/JS/HTML/SCSS/CSS), final newline, trimmed trailing whitespace (not in Markdown).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Concrete formatting settings not in the oracle.

normative_action: File-scoped namespace declarations are suggested for C#.
System directives sorted first; import groups not separated.
IDE0005 (unnecessary usings) is reported at suggestion severity.
var suggested when the type is apparent; explicit types suggested for built-in types; silent elsewhere.
Primary constructors (silent), collection expressions and switch expressions (suggestion), pattern matching (silent).
Braces suggested when multiline; expression-bodied methods on single lines and properties (silent).
I-prefix for interfaces and PascalCase for types and members (suggestion).
Async methods should end in Async (silent severity).
The PreToolUse guard fails closed: internal errors, empty/malformed/mismatched hook input and host-level failures (onFailure block) block the command; Post and Stop failures are advisory (exit 1).

A pending change to SPECIFICATION.md returns feedback to check consistency with CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md and synchronize affected code, tests and docs.
Deleting Directory.Packages.props is an error.
Deleting a package.json produces a warning that dependency removals go through add-dependency.
A change to CLAUDE.md, the register or .claude/ instruction files runs check-instructions and returns its errors (template-maintenance).
Backend production code changed without any backend test change produces a reminder to confirm coverage and probe preservation (verify step 4, development-workflow).

normative_action: Build/test tooling (typescript, vitest, eslint, prettier, jest, @playwright/test, karma, jasmine-core, @types/*) in runtime dependencies produces a warning.

A top-level tests/ directory produces a warning (backend tests live beside production projects).
A frontend package.json without package-lock.json beside it produces a warning.

Approvals for Reserved reference-graph or project changes count only when recorded in a register Accepted-decisions row with a valid ISO date (placeholders do not count), or in a docs/decisions record it links, listing the edge as 'From -> To' or naming the project.

A production project referencing a test project is an error.
A production project referencing a layer outside its allowed set (Domain none; Application→Domain; Infrastructure→Application, Domain; Api→Application, Infrastructure, Domain) is an error.
A test project referencing another test project produces a warning.
Test projects referencing layers beyond their typical scope produce a warning (keep only if required) or an error when forbidden (e.g. Domain.Tests → Infrastructure).
Domain or Application using the Web SDK, the ASP.NET Core shared framework or Microsoft.AspNetCore.* packages is an error.
Frontend package.json entries for @ngrx/*, axios, lodash(-es), bootstrap, @ng-bootstrap/*, ngx-bootstrap or tailwindcss produce a 'not added by default; confirm the concrete need' warning.
Angular build tooling (@angular/cli, @angular/build, @angular-devkit/*, @angular/compiler-cli) in runtime dependencies produces a warning.
Domain or Application referencing Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore packages is an error.
